_comment: Caching-only metadata for the Studio's TTS asset cache — read by the browser bundle (docs/src/components/studio/tts-voice-catalog.ts) and Node tooling (tools/generate-voice-samples.mjs, tools/check-ownership.js's checkVoiceSampleAssets). The VOICE ROSTER itself is NOT here — it's fetched live from OpenRouter's own `supported_voices` field (GET /api/v1/models?output_modalities=speech, via voice-model.js's listOpenRouterVoiceModels()), the single authoritative source every dropdown derives from. This file only says: which live model a cache-directory slug corresponds to (exact modelId match, not a prefix/fuzzy rule — each entry is one pinned model release, not an evolving family), whether it's worth asset-caching at all (requiresAsset), what audio format the provider actually returns (audioFormat — most are mp3; a documented exception declares wav), which of that model's REAL, live-verified voices got a committed sample (cachedVoices — a bounded 'featured' subset per model, not the full roster; every voice still WORKS and appears in the dropdown regardless of whether it's cached, just via the live API instead of an instant local file), and whether the model's `speed` parameter does anything at all (speedSupport). See the redesign section of engineering/decisions/2026-07-09-studio-cloud-ondevice-config-split.md for how this replaced an earlier, doc-scraped static roster (the 'zoe' lesson), and the follow-up section for the speedSupport investigation.

kokoro._note: The one engine that's BOTH on-device and hosted-cloud. On-device (KOKORO_MODEL_ID) is free WASM/WebGPU — no cache needed. But the primary path is HOSTED hexgrad/kokoro-82m via OpenRouter (the connect-time default, and the only Kokoro that works on mobile where the on-device model can't load), which bills per character and — before caching — synthesized live on every Voice-tab audition, a visible per-click delay. Now sample-cached like every other cloud engine: full 54-of-54 live roster (fetched from OpenRouter's own supported_voices for this model id, 2026-07-13). The provider-side timeouts noted in the earlier round of generation have cleared — the endpoint returned a clean 24 kHz mono mp3 for every voice this round. Format is mp3 (no audioFormat override needed).
kokoro._speedNote: Live-tested (2026-07-11): a 0.6x/1.6x request produces audio at ~1/0.6x and ~1/1.6x the baseline duration — matches the requested multiplier almost exactly. Real, accurate, continuous phoneme-duration pacing (kokoro-js's own generate() option on-device, OpenRouter's passthrough param on the hosted endpoint). Errors (422) outside roughly [0.25, 4]; the Studio's UI range (0.75-1.5) sits safely inside that.

grok._note: Full roster (5 of 5) — small enough to cache entirely.
grok._speedNote: Live-tested (2026-07-11): a 0.6x/1.6x request's duration lands within this model's own take-to-take variance (measured ~7% across two identical, speed-less calls) — the `speed` param has no detectable effect. Also absent from this model's `supported_parameters` in OpenRouter's own catalog. Silently ignored, not an error.

gemini._genderNote: Gender is Google's OWN official 'Gender' column for Gemini-TTS (docs.cloud.google.com/text-to-speech/docs/gemini-tts) — 14 female, 16 male across the 30-voice roster — not an ear guess.
gemini._note: Full 30-of-30 live roster cached (2026-07-13) — Gemini is one of the two cheapest, highest-quality engines (with Kokoro), so it earns a complete sample cache. Its voices are bare, language-agnostic names (Puck, Kore, …) with no language or gender encoded in the id, so the voice picker groups them under a single 'All voices' list, not by language. This model's speech endpoint 400s on response_format:"mp3" and only returns raw PCM — the generator requests pcm and wraps it in a WAV container, reading the real sample rate off the response's Content-Type header rather than hardcoding it. The LIVE runtime path (voice-model.js's openRouterRung) had the same mp3-only bug until 2026-07-11 — every real playback/narration through this model 400'd, not just a preview; fixed to mirror the generator's pcm+WAV-wrap for this one model.
gemini._speedNote: Live-tested (2026-07-11): a 0.6x/1.6x request's PCM byte length barely moves (-1% / -7%, versus the 60%+/-40% a real multiplier would produce) — the `speed` param has no meaningful effect. Consistent with Gemini's public API, which controls pace via natural-language style prompts, not a numeric multiplier; OpenRouter's passthrough silently drops it for this model.

orpheus._note: Full live roster (7 of 7) — OpenRouter's own supported_voices field does NOT include "zoe", which an earlier hand-typed roster (sourced from the model's GitHub README, not verified live) wrongly included; that voice consistently 500s on OpenRouter's hosted endpoint. The live field would have caught this from day one.
orpheus._speedNote: Live-tested (2026-07-11): a 0.6x/1.6x request's duration moved BACKWARDS from what a real multiplier would produce (0.6x came out shorter than baseline, 1.6x longer) and stayed within this model's own ~17% take-to-take variance. No detectable effect.

mai-voice-2._note: The ONE engine where OpenRouter's own supported_voices field is a non-exhaustive SAMPLE (4 examples), not the full roster — Microsoft's official docs (learn.microsoft.com/azure/ai-services/speech-service/mai-voices) publish the real 44-voice multilingual roster. voiceOverride supplements the live field with the English-locale voices from that official list, live-verified against OpenRouter's hosted endpoint one by one (format confirmed: "en-US-Harper:MAI-Voice-2", case-insensitive on the locale segment). en-AU-Lisa consistently 502'd on 3 separate live calls (not transient) and is excluded from cachedVoices but kept in voiceOverride so it still appears in the dropdown — OpenRouter's own outage, not ours to hide.
mai-voice-2._speedNote: Live-tested (2026-07-11): a 0.6x/1.6x request produces audio roughly ~2x longer / ~0.7x shorter than baseline — well beyond this model's own ~10% take-to-take variance and in the right direction (Azure's SSML prosody-rate backing this endpoint). Real support, though not a perfectly linear multiplier at the extremes — never errored even at speed=10, but plateaus around a ~1.5s floor by roughly speed=3.

zonos-transformer._note: Live supported_voices also lists "random" (a real, working, non-deterministic option) — deliberately not cached, since a fixed sample would misrepresent a voice whose whole point is to vary. It still appears in the dropdown, just uncached.
zonos-transformer._speedNote: Live-tested (2026-07-11): a 0.6x/1.6x request produces audio ~39% longer / ~32% shorter than baseline — well beyond this model's own ~2% take-to-take variance (the most deterministic of the 9 models tested). Real support. Errors (422) outside roughly [0.25, 4].

zonos-hybrid._note: Same voice namespace and caching rationale as zonos-transformer, above — a separate model/cache directory since it's a distinct live model with potentially different audio quality.
zonos-hybrid._speedNote: Live-tested (2026-07-11): same architecture family and near-identical measured durations as zonos-transformer, above — real support, not independently re-verified past that (see zonos-transformer's own note for the numbers).

csm._note: Full live roster (7 of 7), including "none" (a real, distinct, deterministic no-fixed-persona option — live-verified, not a broken/empty response).
csm._speedNote: Live-tested (2026-07-11): this model's own take-to-take duration variance is enormous (~51% across two identical, speed-less calls) — far larger than any signal a `speed` param could add. The 0.6x/1.6x readings fell entirely inside that noise and in no consistent direction. No usable effect.

voxtral._note: 8-of-30 English-only featured subset (also gb_oliver_*, gb_jane_*, fr_marie_* live and work, just uncached). Mistral's OWN API docs describe voice_id as user-created via voice cloning only — these named presets are real and OpenRouter-published regardless; verified live one by one before caching, not trusted on documentation alone.
voxtral._speedNote: Live-tested (2026-07-11): duration moved BACKWARDS from what a real multiplier would produce and stayed within this model's own ~18% take-to-take variance. No detectable effect.
